title: Record the person's focus and cap urgent/high priorities in the plan
summary: Add an `athena focus` command backed by a new focus record (a directory that does not yet exist at the base commit and is created by this change), shown in `athena status`, plus config caps (3 urgent, 10 high) that make `athena plan` demote the excess items one tier in memory. Audience: the person running Athena, who needs priority to order work again.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust plus the athena.toml setting.
Tests for focus and the caps; cargo test and clippy -D warnings pass.
Behavior criteria name the cargo commands that exercise focus, status and the plan.
Criteria check the demotion lines and the exact count of urgent items, not just that fields exist.
The caps are enforced in the plan code, with config fields in the schema.
One focused change; the steward pass is left out.
Doc comments and the CHANGELOG entry are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-data/src/records.rs (PriorityRecord, PRIORITY_LEVELS, the AnyRecord enum with its validate, path and schema-name match arms, and the records/ allow-list error), crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs (Priority enum, effective_priorities, PlanEntry.priority, priority_violations) and crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs plus crates/athena-core/src/status.rs. A new athena.focus/1 variant must be added to AnyRecord with validate, path and schema arms so check_record_file and the AnyRecord round-trip test accept it; the producer must extend that round-trip test. The cap is measured directly on the order and tiers `athena plan` produces, not through a stand-in.

The records/focus/ directory does not exist at the base commit; this change introduces it at runtime through the new record path (records/ is never edited by hand and no files are committed there). Focus record path pattern is assumed to be records/focus/<month>/<id>.json, like other month-sharded records, with fields text and set_by.
Latest focus record means the greatest id (time-ordered). 'Set by' is taken from the same identity source other person-written records use, such as the priority record.

Caps live in athena.toml under a new section, with a defaults-bearing field in crates/athena-data/src/config.rs (urgent_cap = 3, high_cap = 10). Demotion is computed in memory in plan.rs on effective priorities: urgent excess goes to high, then high excess (including those demoted) goes to normal. Kept order: items whose priority was set by a person record first (most recent first), then the rest in plan order. Items with a person's priority record are never demoted below their own record.
Each demoted item prints one line in `athena plan` output; no request or priority record is rewritten.
The steward triage pass that uses focus is a separate request and is not built here.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: a CLI test runs `athena focus "speed first"`, then asserts a focus record file is written under the new focus records directory (created by the test's temp repo), that `athena focus` prints "speed first", and that `athena status` output contains it.
Run `cargo test`: a test sets a second focus after the first and asserts `athena focus` and `athena status` print only the later text.

Run `cargo test`: a plan test with 5 urgent items asserts exactly 3 are treated as urgent, a person-set urgent item (via a priority record) is among those 3, and the plan output has one demotion line for each of the 2 demoted items.

Run `cargo test`: a test asserts the high cap of 10 demotes excess high items to normal, and that a person's priority record still wins for its own item; no request or priority record file is modified by planning.
athena.toml sets the urgent cap to 3 and the high cap to 10, and crates/athena-data/src/config.rs declares the matching schema fields with those defaults; Grep shows both.
crates/athena-data/src/records.rs adds the focus record to AnyRecord with validation (non-empty text and set_by), a path and a schema name, and the AnyRecord round-trip test covers it.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing `athena focus`, the status line and the priority caps.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`: all pass.

out_of_scope: The steward triage pass that uses the focus (a separate request)
Re-tiering or rewriting existing queue items or priority records
Editing anything under records/ by hand
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass probability than the reference: the change touches a record enum, config, plan ordering and the CLI together.
hard_reason: Adds a cap rule that changes how the plan ranks and demotes work, which is part of the run pipeline and hard to see when wrong.
